name: Bayview Hunters Point
blurb: The southeast waterfront: a former naval shipyard, Third Street's shops and restored wetlands at Heron's Head.

name: Bernal Heights
blurb: A hilltop village of narrow streets crowned by a bald, windy summit and its little tower, Sutrito.

name: Castro/Upper Market
blurb: The heart of LGBTQ San Francisco, home of the Castro Theatre, Harvey Milk Plaza and Dolores Park's sunny slope.

name: Chinatown
blurb: The oldest Chinatown in North America, packed with alleys, temples, dim sum and the Dragon Gate.

name: Excelsior
blurb: A family neighborhood on the city's southern edge, with streets named for countries and world capitals.

name: Financial District/South Beach
blurb: Downtown towers built on Gold Rush landfill, from the Transamerica Pyramid to Salesforce Tower and the Ferry Building.

name: Glen Park
blurb: A small village around a BART station and a wild canyon where Islais Creek still runs free.

name: Golden Gate Park
blurb: Over a thousand acres of forest, lakes, museums, windmills and bison, grown on former sand dunes.

name: Haight Ashbury
blurb: Victorian streets that hosted the 1967 Summer of Love, beside the city's oldest official park.

name: Hayes Valley
blurb: Boutiques and the Civic Center arts district, stretching west to Alamo Square and the Painted Ladies.

name: Inner Richmond
blurb: The foggy avenues north of Golden Gate Park, famous for Clement Street's dim sum and dumplings.

name: Inner Sunset
blurb: A lively strip on Irving and 9th, climbing into Golden Gate Heights and its famous tiled stairways.

name: Japantown
blurb: One of the last three Japantowns in the United States, centered on the Peace Pagoda.

name: Lakeshore
blurb: The southwest corner around Lake Merced, San Francisco State and the hang gliding cliffs of Fort Funston.

name: Lincoln Park
blurb: Cypress-covered clifftops at the city's northwest tip, home of the Legion of Honor and the Lands End trail.

name: Lone Mountain/USF
blurb: The hilltop campus of the University of San Francisco, on land once covered by Victorian cemeteries.

name: Marina
blurb: Bayfront flats built on 1915 world's fair landfill, with the Palace of Fine Arts and the Wave Organ.

name: McLaren Park
blurb: A big, quiet park of ridges, groves and reservoirs, with an amphitheater named for Jerry Garcia.

name: Mission
blurb: The sunny, mural-covered heart of Latino San Francisco and the home of the Mission burrito.

name: Mission Bay
blurb: A new neighborhood of labs and apartments on old rail yards, home of Chase Center and Oracle Park.

name: Nob Hill
blurb: The hill of railroad barons, grand hotels, Grace Cathedral and the cable car powerhouse.

name: Noe Valley
blurb: A sunny valley of strollers and cafes on 24th Street, tucked between steep hills.

name: North Beach
blurb: Little Italy and Beat Generation headquarters, rising up Telegraph Hill to Coit Tower and down to the Wharf.

name: Oceanview/Merced/Ingleside
blurb: Residential neighborhoods along the M and K streetcar lines near the city's southern border.

name: Outer Mission
blurb: A working neighborhood along Mission Street's southern stretch, toward Daly City.

name: Outer Richmond
blurb: Foggy avenues running to the ocean, ending at the Cliff House, Sutro Baths and Sutro Heights.

name: Pacific Heights
blurb: Mansions and grand views along a ridge above the Marina, crossed by the Lyon Street Steps.

name: Portola
blurb: Once the city's garden district, where greenhouses grew flowers for the whole city.

name: Potrero Hill
blurb: A sunny hill with skyline views and Vermont Street, a block even curvier than Lombard.

name: Presidio
blurb: A former Army post turned national park, with forests, beaches, Crissy Field and the Golden Gate Bridge.

name: Presidio Heights
blurb: Quiet, leafy streets of grand homes along the Presidio's southern wall.

name: Russian Hill
blurb: Steep lanes, hidden stairways and Lombard Street's switchbacks, with the Hyde Street cable car on top.

name: Seacliff
blurb: Oceanfront homes above China Beach and Baker Beach, facing the Golden Gate.

name: South of Market
blurb: Warehouses turned startups, museums and nightclubs, where much of the city's tech boom was born.

name: Sunset/Parkside
blurb: Miles of pastel houses on old sand dunes, ending at Ocean Beach and the new Sunset Dunes park.

name: Tenderloin
blurb: A dense, historic downtown neighborhood beside City Hall and the Powell Street cable car turntable.

name: Treasure Island
blurb: A man-made island built for the 1939 world's fair, joined to natural Yerba Buena Island mid-bay.

name: Twin Peaks
blurb: The windy summits near the city's center, with Sutro Tower rising behind them.

name: Visitacion Valley
blurb: A diverse valley at the southern edge of the city, bordering McLaren Park and San Bruno Mountain.

name: West of Twin Peaks
blurb: Garden suburbs born when the Twin Peaks Tunnel opened in 1918, below Mount Davidson's cross.

name: Western Addition
blurb: The historic Fillmore, once the Harlem of the West, and home of the Fillmore Auditorium.
